ambiguities.text: The specification does not define what happens when more than MAX_EXECUTION_PROOFS_PER_PAYLOAD (4) proofs are received for the same payload.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume that only the first 4 valid proofs per payload are stored and subsequent proofs are silently dropped. This is consistent with the uniqueness check on (root, type, prover_pubkey) tuples.

ambiguities.text: The ordering of gossip validation checks is not explicitly specified as mandatory in the given sequence.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume implementations may reorder checks for efficiency (e.g., check signature last as it is most expensive), as long as all checks are performed before acceptance.

implicit_assumptions.description: The gossip validation pipeline assumes the beacon state used to check active validator status is sufficiently recent and consistent across nodes.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Nodes with stale state could accept proofs from validators that have been ejected, or reject proofs from newly activated validators, causing gossip inconsistency.

implicit_assumptions.description: An attacker cannot forge BLS signatures for active validators without possessing their private keys.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Forged execution proofs could be propagated through the network, potentially causing nodes to accept invalid execution results.

implicit_assumptions.description: The gossipsub mesh provides sufficient connectivity for execution proofs to propagate to all interested nodes in a timely manner.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Execution proofs could be delayed or lost, reducing confidence in execution validity across the network.
